IR.rationale: A rising 1-year yield relative to Fed Funds signals expected tightening, which raises funding costs and lowers risk appetite and leveraged-strategy returns. Its absence is the benign rate state.

B.rationale: Stable or falling high-yield and EM corporate yields describe easy credit conditions. That supports the carry, credit and event-driven exposures common to hedge funds.

V.rationale: News-based financial-crisis volatility captures funding and deleveraging risk that hits arbitrage and credit-sensitive strategies with a lag.

AP.rationale: Hedge-fund indices carry net equity beta and report with stale prices. Strong US and EM equity returns therefore mark a broad risk-on state that carries into subsequent fund returns.

TF.rationale: Large payoffs to short-rate trend-following straddles indicate disorderly rate moves (Fung-Hsieh). Such moves tend to precede weaker returns for non-directional strategies.

ST.rationale: Profitable liquidity provision (high reversal returns) without a flight to quality (low RMW) describes a calm market. In that state arbitrageurs earn their liquidity premium.

FX.rationale: A broadly weakening dollar alongside a firm carry/commodity currency signals global risk appetite and easy dollar funding.

COM.rationale: Rising copper prices proxy global growth momentum, which supports risk assets and hedge-fund betas.

MC.rationale: Loose financial conditions combined with above-trend activity is the macro state in which leverage is cheap and risk premia are harvested successfully.

ENDG.rationale: Hedge-fund returns are positively autocorrelated because of illiquid holdings, return smoothing and persistent capital flows.

IR.rationale: Rising bill rates tighten funding liquidity for levered strategies and raise the risk of forced deleveraging.

B.rationale: Joint widening in European and US high-yield markets signals a global credit shock. Such shocks drive tail losses in credit, distressed and convertible-arbitrage strategies.

V.rationale: Crisis-related volatility indicates funding stress and crowded-trade unwinds, which raise the probability of large drawdowns.

AP.rationale: Weak EM equities signal global risk-off and dollar-funding strain that spills into hedge-fund losses.

TF.rationale: Large short-rate trend payoffs reflect rate shocks that hurt fixed-income arbitrage and levered carry positions.

ST.rationale: A flight to quality combined with losses on liquidity provision marks a liquidity crunch in which arbitrage capital is withdrawn.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength and a falling carry currency signal tightening global dollar liquidity and carry unwinds.

COM.rationale: Falling oil prices signal weakening demand and stress in energy credit, which feeds tail losses in credit and event-driven books.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with weak activity is the classic macro setting for deleveraging and large losses.

ENDG.rationale: Because of return smoothing and the momentum of redemptions, recent poor returns make further large losses more likely.

IR.rationale: The absence of tightening expectations eases funding costs and supports strong risk-asset rallies.

B.rationale: Easing EM corporate yields signal global credit relief and capital inflows, which favour large gains in credit-sensitive strategies.

V.rationale: An elevated VIX carries high risk premia and wide arbitrage spreads, so subsequent upside tails are fatter once stress abates.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equities combined with growth leadership describe a risk-on regime in which net-long hedge funds post large gains.

TF.rationale: Calm short-rate markets let carry and arbitrage positions compound without disruption.

ST.rationale: No flight to quality signals risk appetite in which junk and levered positions rally strongly.

FX.rationale: A strengthening carry/commodity currency signals global risk-on and profitable carry trades.

COM.rationale: Copper strength reflects global growth momentum that supports upside in risk-sensitive strategies.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress leaves distressed and arbitrage spreads wide, so the subsequent normalisation can produce large gains.

ENDG.rationale: Positive autocorrelation from smoothing and from inflows chasing performance makes large gains more likely after strong recent returns.
